scope: Linux Chromium browser process tree; natural collection; not native desktop or hardware GPU results
limitation: Final code additionally preserves one oversized PDF undo snapshot; this change was regression tested separately, not re-profiled. Physical recycling is asynchronous and active Office memory remains high.

runs.label: baseline-complete

methodology.graphics: headless Chromium, SwiftShader software WebGL; not a hardware GPU comparison
methodology.processes: SystemInfo.getProcessInfo plus descendants of its browser PID; browser renderer GPU utility and zygote included
methodology.physicalMetric: Sum of /proc/PID/smaps_rollup Pss; USS=Private_Clean+Private_Dirty+Private_Hugetlb. RSS may double-count shared pages.
methodology.gc: Natural sample after fixed settle, then optional CDP page collection plus exposed gc in frames. Pthread workers may block JS execution and are not explicitly collected. Later stages follow earlier page GC.
methodology.excludes: Vite/Node harness/Python PDF backend process memory; WASM byteLength is recorded separately and never added to physical totals.

measurementNotes: The initial benchmark's sharedWasm field used instanceof across the parent/iframe realm and incorrectly reports false. This field is invalid for this run; the pinned WASM import independently requires shared=true. Physical /proc counters, heap byteLength, and thread counts are unaffected. The reporter is corrected for subsequent runs.

Forced worker GC was abandoned during separate unsuccessful harness runs because pthread workers may block JS evaluation. This complete baseline uses natural samples only, MEMORY_GC=0, with five seconds of settling at each stage.

Export content validation was performed independently on the saved baseline artifacts after browser exit: both DOCX files contain COMPAT-WORD-RICH; spreadsheet has a 2001-row sheet; PPTX and exported PDF each have 20 pages/slides. Subsequent runs perform these same checks inline.
